objective: Promote one pinned Qwen3-VL 8B Thinking Q4_K_M Ollama checkpoint as Hina's text reasoning brain with a same-weight fast path for routine chat, move explicit screen reading behind a separately configurable Ollama Cloud or lightweight Ollama local vision provider, persist the Cloud key only through Electron OS-backed safeStorage, and add an explicit owner-controlled game-session snapshot archive for higher-quality historical re-analysis.
non_goals: Do not load a second text-brain checkpoint, continuously record the screen, autonomously act on image output or automatically write image output to memory.
Do not treat an archived image as a current observation after the existing maximum-15-second TTL expires.
Do not persist OCR text, VLM output, prompts, chat content or raw public input beside archived PNG files.
Do not fine-tune, distill or change model weights in this slice.
Do not store an Ollama Cloud key in source, Git, logs, browser storage, plaintext files or renderer-readable status.
Do not permit a local screen-reading model above the lightweight 5 GB/approximately 5B boundary in this slice.
contracts: qwen3-vl:8b-thinking-q4_K_M is the only configured text-brain checkpoint; routine text uses a same-weight pre-closed-thought path, complex text uses bounded hidden thinking, and untrusted text cannot inject Qwen control tokens into the raw template.
Perception never routes screen images through the text-brain gateway. It uses a separate runtime-configurable Ollama Cloud or Ollama local vision boundary.

Ollama Cloud requests use only the fixed https://ollama.com API endpoint; the bearer key is decrypted by Electron main, passed to loopback runtime memory, and never returned in status, errors or renderer-readable persistence state.
Electron persists provider/model plus only an OS-encrypted safeStorage ciphertext under userData, restores it after restart and changes or clears it only after an explicit operator action.
Ollama local discovery uses /api/tags plus /api/show and returns only models advertising vision that satisfy the lightweight profile; inference uses the shared scheduler and keep_alive=0.
Complex text reasoning is never emitted to UI, logs or TTS and the complete brain request has a hard 10-second deadline.

The Ollama profile requests full GPU offload and every real acceptance smoke must observe 100% GPU execution; unavailable GPU capacity fails visibly rather than selecting another model or CPU fallback.
Snapshot archiving is available but inactive by default, starts only after an explicit owner action and stores only validated PNG bytes under a fixed physical repository-local root.
An archive session is bound to the owner console session, bounded by byte and snapshot quotas, and exposes no caller-controlled filesystem path.
Stopping an archive prevents future writes but deliberately leaves its PNG files for the owner to inspect and manually remove after the game session.
Historical re-analysis never enters the fresh observation ledger or memory and always returns historical=true plus decisionSupportEligible=false.
The shared scheduler serializes the text brain, optional local vision, STT, TTS and OCR GPU work and preserves at least 2048 MiB headroom; Ollama Cloud vision consumes zero local model VRAM.
allowed_dependencies: Existing Python and Node standard libraries, Electron safeStorage, Hina resource scheduler, Ollama 0.32.5 local/cloud APIs and existing browser APIs; no new package dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Model config/provider tests pin qwen3-vl:8b-thinking-q4_K_M, an 8192-token runtime context, Q4-oriented VRAM reservation, full GPU offload request, bounded fast/thinking budgets, a hard 10-second request deadline and deterministic keep_alive=0 unload.
Tests prove simple text uses the same-weight pre-closed-thought path, complex text uses native thinking, control tokens are neutralized and hidden reasoning is never yielded as assistant text.
A real simple text smoke and complex reasoning smoke return non-empty Vietnamese output within 10 seconds while Ollama reports 100% GPU execution.

Vision provider tests prove Cloud authentication never appears in status/errors, local discovery filters by the advertised vision capability, oversized local models are rejected and local inference owns a scheduler lease.
Desktop tests prove operator-only IPC, OS safeStorage encryption, bounded strict persistence and automatic provider restoration without exposing decrypted key material to the renderer.

Perception unit and route tests prove archive default-off behavior, owner-session binding, fixed-root containment, exclusive bounded writes, quota rejection, stop semantics and historical re-analysis isolation.

The desktop Quan sat dashboard lets a non-developer enter or replace an Ollama Cloud key, discover only vision-capable models, select Cloud or a lightweight local model and understand the privacy/VRAM tradeoff.

The Dev Console Quan sat page lets a non-developer start/stop an image-retention session, shows the exact local folder/count/bytes and clearly distinguishes current TTL observations from retained history.
A real serialized OCR, 8B text brain, Moonshine STT and OmniVoice TTS run records peak physical GPU use below 14336 MiB and at least 2048 MiB free VRAM; Cloud vision adds no local model VRAM.
One-off scripts, raw benchmark screenshots/audio and pull logs are removed after concise metrics and provenance are recorded.
required_test_commands: $env:PYTHONPATH='apps/core-runtime/src;packages/contracts/src;packages/safety-policy/src;packages/text-brain/src;workers/perception/src'; uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s apps/core-runtime/tests -p "test_perception_routes.py"
